title: Ruby Measures the Tallest Flower
markdown:
Mr. Clive’s garden was full of plants and pretty flowers. Ruby the shape spotter loved visiting. She saw squares in the path, circles in the flower pots, and triangles in the leaves. It was like a big shape puzzle.

Her best friend Dash the dog loved the garden too. He bounced and wagged. His floppy ears flew when he ran.

One sunny afternoon, Ruby looked up, way up. “Look at the sunflowers, Dash!” Dash wagged. Sunflowers were like giant happy yellow faces.

“This one is tall,” Ruby said, pointing. “But look at that one!” She pointed to another sunflower, even taller. Its yellow face seemed to reach for the sky.

Ruby made a little thinking face. “How do we know which one is really the tallest? I can’t just guess!” She paced, brow a little crinkled. Dash sniffed a ladybug.

Then Ruby saw a long piece of garden twine. A happy idea popped. “Dash! Come here!” Dash bounded over, tail a blur.

Ruby carefully held one end of the twine at the bottom of the first tall sunflower. The twine went all the way up to the top of its fuzzy head. “See, Dash? This piece of twine is as tall as this sunflower.”

Then she stood the twine up straight next to Dash. It reached all the way up to his floppy ears. “So this sunflower is about as tall as Dash, from the ground to his ears. The twine tells us so, because it matches both.”

Dash stood as tall as he could next to the giant sunflower. The sunflower was still much, much taller. Ruby held the same twine up beside it. It didn’t quite reach the very top. She needed a little more twine.

She found another piece. She held it up next to the first piece, making one long line. Now the two pieces of twine together were exactly as tall as the giant sunflower. She measured carefully.

“Mr. Clive!” Ruby ran to the kind gardener who was looking after his roses. Dash trotted beside her. “We found the tallest sunflower! And we used a special way to know!”

Mr. Clive smiled. “Oh? And what was that, Ruby?”

“We measured it!” Ruby held up her two pieces of twine. “We used the twine to see how tall it was. The first sunflower was one twine tall. This one is two.”

Mr. Clive chuckled. “That’s wonderful. You were measuring the height of the sunflowers. Height is how tall something is. When you used the twine, you were seeing how many twine-lengths the sunflower was. That’s like using a ruler. Rulers help us measure and compare sizes.”

He knelt down. “Every time you compare something to see how tall it is, you’re measuring.”

Ruby looked at the giant sunflower, then at her twine, then at Dash. Two twines. One tallest flower. Dash sat under it, ears still floppy, and Ruby wound the twine back into a neat coil, ready for the next height that needed a number instead of a guess.
